steps.title: Validate the experiment
steps.explanation: Accept only a fixed lesson mode. Browser configuration cannot supply arbitrary paths, endpoints, tool definitions or approval decisions.
steps.narration: Step 1. Accept only a fixed lesson mode. Browser configuration cannot supply arbitrary paths, endpoints, tool definitions or approval decisions. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Copy fictional helpdesk data
steps.explanation: Each run copies a tracked fictional seed into its own ignored runtime JSON. No external helpdesk or real customer is contacted.
steps.narration: Step 2. Each run copies a tracked fictional seed into its own ignored runtime JSON. No external helpdesk or real customer is contacted. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Define the read tool and error response
steps.explanation: tool() declares a bounded ticket ID and read-only annotation. The shared wrapper returns isError for controlled tool failures, preserving an actual MCP result.
steps.narration: Step 3. tool() declares a bounded ticket ID and read-only annotation. The shared wrapper returns isError for controlled tool failures, preserving an actual MCP result. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Separate safe tools from the sender
steps.explanation: Only the two reads and local tagging tool are automatically allowed. send_reply is deliberately absent so native permissions can ask the reviewer.
steps.narration: Step 4. Only the two reads and local tagging tool are automatically allowed. send_reply is deliberately absent so native permissions can ask the reviewer. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Start the real query with bounded options
steps.explanation: Use a real SDK query, default permission mode, isolated settings, finite turns and an estimate threshold. No built-in tool or wildcard sender permission is exposed.
anchors: const run = query({ prompt: input(), options });
steps.narration: Step 5. Use a real SDK query, default permission mode, isolated settings, finite turns and an estimate threshold. No built-in tool or wildcard sender permission is exposed. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Wait on the native reply permission
steps.explanation: canUseTool receives the actual ticket, draft and native tool-use ID. It waits on a pending browser approval request; reads and tagging did not wait for this callback.
steps.narration: Step 6. canUseTool receives the actual ticket, draft and native tool-use ID. It waits on a pending browser approval request; reads and tagging did not wait for this callback. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Register the one-use approval request
steps.explanation: Register before emitting the SSE request so a fast reviewer response is not lost. Abort or timeout rejects and removes the waiter. This local teaching UI has no production reviewer authentication.
steps.narration: Step 7. Register before emitting the SSE request so a fast reviewer response is not lost. Abort or timeout rejects and removes the waiter. This local teaching UI has no production reviewer authentication. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Validate and resolve the browser decision
steps.explanation: The bounded same-origin JSON route accepts only an existing approval ID and a valid decision. A stale or replayed ID returns 409. Reviewers cannot change the ticket ID.
steps.narration: Step 8. The bounded same-origin JSON route accepts only an existing approval ID and a valid decision. A stale or replayed ID returns 409. Reviewers cannot change the ticket ID. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Apply the reviewer edit through updatedInput
steps.explanation: Reject returns the SDK native deny response. Approve or edit grants one exact ticket/body pair and returns updatedInput for that same ticket.
steps.narration: Step 9. Reject returns the SDK native deny response. Approve or edit grants one exact ticket/body pair and returns updatedInput for that same ticket. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Record only the exact approved reply
steps.explanation: The handler independently consumes a one-use grant. A changed body or unapproved call is refused. It records only local JSON and explicitly reports that no real message was sent.
steps.narration: Step 10. The handler independently consumes a one-use grant. A changed body or unapproved call is refused. It records only local JSON and explicitly reports that no real message was sent. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Observe actual post-tool results
steps.explanation: The native PostToolUse hook records actual tool input and response. Audit records complement the local JSON and reviewer decision; a successful tag is not a sent reply.
steps.narration: Step 11. The native PostToolUse hook records actual tool input and response. Audit records complement the local JSON and reviewer decision; a successful tag is not a sent reply. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Preserve results and validate typed triage
steps.explanation: Validate the actual structured output with Zod. A missing field or invalid summary stays a validation error. Batch preserves separate native query results and sessions.
steps.narration: Step 12. Validate the actual structured output with Zod. A missing field or invalid summary stays a validation error. Batch preserves separate native query results and sessions. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Check approvals against persisted replies
steps.explanation: Every recorded reply must exactly match an approve/edit decision for its ticket. Retain helpdesk.json and audit.json, then remove only the disposable SDK workspace.
steps.narration: Step 13. Every recorded reply must exactly match an approve/edit decision for its ticket. Retain helpdesk.json and audit.json, then remove only the disposable SDK workspace. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.
